title: Pause a tool action, approve it, then replay offline
summary: Watch a generated native agent stop before a write, approve the exact action, and replay it after its services have stopped.
prerequisites: Complete the repository installation: Node.js 22+, npm ci, then npm run build.
Use Bash or another POSIX shell on macOS/Linux; use WSL on Windows. Run commands from the cloned repository root.
The checked-in verify.mjs helper only reads the tutorial outputs and checks the expected facts. All agent actions still use the visible Instrilo commands.
outcome: A completed durable run, a Mermaid run graph, and matched replay with zero live calls.

verification.scope: The CLI and actual generated native TypeScript runtime execute against local deterministic model/read/write fixtures.
limitations: The fixture write changes only a local in-memory counter, not an external system.
This is local durable execution under OS file permissions; it is not a hosted multi-user approval service.
Recording stores task/model/tool content. Inspect records before sharing; scrubbing cannot guarantee removal of every possible secret.

steps.title: Start a controlled read/write example
steps.body: The deterministic model proposes lookup(42), then update(42, ready). The update tool explicitly requires approval.
steps.code:
set -eu
INSTRILO_PROJECT=.studio/tutorials/approvals-and-replay
node dist/cli.js init approvals-and-replay --directory .studio/tutorials
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/fixture.mjs "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.log" 2>&1 &
INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID=$!
trap 'kill "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/control.mjs "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture" ready
node dist/cli.js connections add local-tools "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture/tools-runtime.json"
node dist/cli.js connections use runtime local-tools "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js tools add "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture/lookup.json"
node dist/cli.js tools add "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture/update.json"
node dist/cli.js build "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js prepare "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: The generated runtime has one read tool and one approval-required write tool, both confined to the local fixture.

steps.title: Record the run and verify the pause
steps.body: Content recording is explicit. Exit 3 means paused before the write, not completed. The fixture counter proves the write has not happened.
steps.code:
INSTRILO_RUN_EXIT=0
node dist/cli.js runs start "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --input 'Inspect record 42 and set its state to ready.' --record-content > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/paused.json" || INSTRILO_RUN_EXIT=$?
test "$INSTRILO_RUN_EXIT" -eq 3
INSTRILO_RUN_ID=$(node -p 'require("./"+process.argv[1]+"/paused.json").id' "$INSTRILO_PROJECT")
node dist/cli.js approvals show "$INSTRILO_RUN_ID" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/pending.json"
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/control.mjs "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture" counts > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/before-counts.json"
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/verify.mjs approval-pause "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: The pending record names update and its exact arguments/digest. Counters show one read and zero writes.

steps.title: Approve that exact digest and resume
steps.body: For this tutorial, inspect the displayed request and confirm it targets only the in-memory fixture. Approval is bound to the action and expires after five minutes; it does not resume work automatically.
steps.code:
INSTRILO_APPROVAL_DIGEST=$(node -p 'require("./"+process.argv[1]+"/pending.json").pending[0].approvalDigest' "$INSTRILO_PROJECT")
node dist/cli.js approvals approve "$INSTRILO_RUN_ID" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --digest "$INSTRILO_APPROVAL_DIGEST" --expires-in 300 --reviewer 'Tutorial operator'
node dist/cli.js runs resume "$INSTRILO_RUN_ID" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/completed.json"
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/control.mjs "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture" counts > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/after-counts.json"
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/verify.mjs approved-run "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js runs graph "$INSTRILO_RUN_ID" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/run.mmd"
steps.expected: The run completes, with one read and exactly one fixture write. run.mmd describes its model/tool steps.

steps.title: Stop every fixture service and replay
steps.body: Frozen replay consumes recorded model/tool responses. Stopping the service first makes an accidental live dependency visible.
steps.code:
kill "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID"
wait "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID" || true
trap - EXIT
node dist/cli.js runs replay "$INSTRILO_RUN_ID" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/replay.json"
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/verify.mjs offline-replay "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: matched:true, modelCalls:0, and toolCalls:0. The saved run remains available for inspection without a running service.

troubleshooting: Use a fresh tutorial project name if init says the directory already exists. The commands create files and reports that deliberately refuse overwriting existing results.
Read the printed error and instrilo help --all before retrying. A failed assertion means the observed result differs from this guide.
If approval expires, this run cannot silently renew it. Start a fresh controlled run and inspect the new digest.
A changed build rejects resume/replay. Keep the original build or create a new run; do not alter recorded hashes.
If a real external write has an ambiguous result, inspect that system before using approvals reconcile. Never blindly retry it.
cleanup: The tutorial creates only its named project under .studio/tutorials. Keep reports if useful; remove that project directory when you no longer need it.
